archetype.name: Rebuilding (fast and leaky)
archetype.definition: A Chicago team with no roster group graded above C-, a bottom-three defense and a margin that, not bad luck, puts it among the league's worst, sliding further from the .500-ish level it held a few years ago.

report.headline: A 3-9 start earned honestly, built on an open paint and cold threes
report.take:
Start with what the record is not: unlucky. The Bulls' W vs Pt Diff is 0 and their wins by differential is 3, exactly the three games they have won. The net rating of -10.9 ranks 26th, the defense rates 121.0 points per 100 possessions (28th) and the offense 110.1 (25th). This is a continuation of a slide, not a blip. Chicago went 39-43 in 2023-24 and 2024-25, fell to 31-51 with a -5.1 net rating last season, and has roughly doubled that deficit through 12 games. The site has them 28th of 30, and the grades back it up: backcourt D-, wings D+, frontcourt C-.

The pace distorts the per-game view in both directions. Chicago plays at 103.2, well above the league's 98.9. That inflates the scoring to 114.58 a game, which ranks a respectable 15th, while the efficiency behind it ranks 25th. It also makes the defense look like the worst in the league at 125.92 allowed (30th), when per possession it is 'only' 28th. The real defensive problem is structural. Opponents take 38.4% of their shots at the rim, the highest share in the league and 8.9 points above average. Chicago forces turnovers on just 11.8% of plays (27th) and grabs only 69.4% of defensive rebounds (26th). Teams get where they want, keep the ball, and get second chances. Opposing point guards have feasted, scoring 29.42 a game and 4.82 above their own averages, the second-worst mark in the league against that position.

There is a hidden cushion and a hidden trap. The cushion is the jumper. Chicago takes 45.5% of its shots from three (10th) but hits 31.1%, dead last. Its last two seasons sat at 35.6% and 36.7% on similar volume, so some of that should come back. The trap is at the rim: opponents shoot only 62.0% there (4th best). On that much volume, that number is more likely to drift toward the league's 65.1 than hold. If it does, the defense gets worse even as the shooting gets better.

The recent stretch is the one encouraging thread. October went 1-5 with 129.33 allowed a game. November is 2-4 with 122.5 allowed. The last five games were played at -4.4 a game, 6.93 better than the season, capped by an overtime win over Atlanta and a 117-106 win at Minnesota that ended an eight-game skid. That is a team getting less bad, not a team turning a corner. The frontcourt is also thinning: Caleb Wilson, the leading frontcourt scorer, is out, and Jalen Smith, the most productive player on the sheet, is day-to-day.

strengths.title: Living at the free-throw line
strengths.body: Chicago's FT Rate of 32.4 ranks 5th, far above the 24.6 it posted last season and the 21.4 the year before. That is a real change in how the offense attacks, not a hot streak, and it is the main reason the true shooting (56.1%) holds up better than the three-point percentage. Free-throw drawing tends to be sticky, so this should last, though losing Wilson's usage will test it.

strengths.title: Smith and Powell score efficiently
strengths.body: Jalen Smith is the best player on the sheet by the site's own measure (17th of 92 centers), with a 62.2 TS %, a 1.5 BPM and a team-high 0.8 Win Shares, and the team is better with him on the floor. Norman Powell carries the most usage among the guards (27.3%) at a 60.3 TS % and leads the team in points. Neither is the problem; the issue is how little efficient scoring surrounds them.

concerns.title: The paint is wide open
concerns.body: Opponents take the league's highest share of shots at the rim, and Chicago doesn't end possessions with turnovers or defensive rebounds either. That combination produces a 121.0 defensive rating. The only thing propping it up is opponents' unusually poor finishing at the rim, which is the likeliest number on the sheet to turn against them. Without better point-of-attack containment, this stays a bottom-five defense.

concerns.title: Volume threes without the accuracy
concerns.body: Chicago takes threes like a top-10 team and makes them like the worst. History says the 31.1% is too low for this shooting profile, so expect improvement. But Josh Giddey (50.4 TS %) and Isaac Okoro (52.1) play heavy minutes without spacing the floor, which keeps the ceiling modest.

concerns.title: Frontcourt depth is about to be tested
concerns.body: Wilson is out and Smith is day-to-day. The fallback options have been the roster's worst: Zach Collins has a 33.4 TS % and a -14.4 On-Off, and Noa Essengue has a -8.2 BPM. Patrick Williams has a +20.5 On-Off and a 65.1 TS %, but in only five games, so he is a hope rather than a fix.

trend.note: Points allowed per game fell from 129.33 in October to 122.5 in November, and the last five games ran 6.93 points a game better than the season. That is a modest climb from a very low floor, and Wilson's absence could stall it.

weekAhead.headline: Cleveland twice and Denver, with Wilson out and a back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
Five games, three of them against teams with real offenses. Cleveland (7-7, 12th on the site) runs a 117.8 offensive rating, 7th in the league, and gets both ends of the week: in Cleveland Monday, then in Chicago on the second night of a back-to-back after Denver visits. The Nuggets (7-4) bring an A backcourt and turn it over on just 12.1% of plays. That is a bad fit for a defense that already forces the fewest turnovers in the league outside a handful of teams.

The middle of the week is where the wins are. Brooklyn is 3-9 with a 116.8 defensive rating, and Washington, who beat Chicago 120-124 at the United Center in October, is 4-10. Both have weaknesses Chicago's shape can attack. Realistically this is a one- or two-win week, with the Nets and Wizards games deciding which.

keyMatchups.title: Smith's health versus Cleveland's bigs
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's A- frontcourt meets a Chicago interior already allowing the most rim attempts in the league. The Cavaliers also leak production to centers, allowing 22.71 points a game there, among the most in the league. If Smith plays, that is an opening; if he doesn't, the minutes go to Collins and the matchup flips hard.

keyMatchups.title: Buzelis against Washington's wings
keyMatchups.body: Washington allows 29.21 points a game to small forwards, the most in the league, behind an F-graded wing group. Matas Buzelis (59.9 TS %) is Chicago's most efficient high-minute wing and should be the focal point that night. The Wizards also rebound poorly, so the offensive glass should be there too.

keyMatchups.title: Attacking Brooklyn's soft rim
keyMatchups.body: Brooklyn's opponents shoot 68.8% at the rim (25th), which suits a Chicago team that lives at the line. The catch is the guards. The Nets hold point guards to 20.25 points a game, the fewest in the league, so Giddey's lane may close and the scoring has to come from Powell and the forwards.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Chicago can keep Cleveland out of the paint twice in eight days; the rim-attempt share is the defense's whole story.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace points to about 21 wins. There is reason to expect slightly better: the three-point shooting is far below this group's recent history, and the November defense has been meaningfully less bad than October's. The free-throw rate looks like a real, lasting change. What won't hold is the rim finishing against them. Opponents shooting this poorly on this many rim attempts is a gift, and as it fades it will eat into whatever the jumpers give back. With no roster group above C- and the frontcourt banged up, the realistic range is a 22-28 win season, with a defense that stays in the bottom five and an offense that climbs a few spots toward the low 110s.

Nothing here suggests a play-in push. The margin is honest and the division already has three teams comfortably ahead. The more useful questions are developmental: whether Buzelis keeps his efficiency on more usage, and whether the Williams minutes are a real signal.
swingFactors: How far the 3P % bounces back toward last season's level

confidence.note: 12 games is small, but the margin matches the record and the defensive profile is extreme enough to trust its direction.
